column2: Where the name is printed on the physical card (its upper left corner) is card layout; the engine takes each card's name from the Oracle card reference, so there is nothing to execute. Names themselves are tested under 201.2-201.6.

Describes the interchangeable names indicator printed on later printings (bottom left corner); printing information not in the card data. Interchangeable names are tested under 201.3, 201.3a, 201.3b and 201.4g.

The expansion symbol identifies the set of a printing and "has no effect on game play"; it isn't a characteristic and the engine's Oracle card data has none. Rules about names originally printed in a set are tested under 206.3.
The color of the expansion symbol indicates the printing's rarity; printed information with no effect on game play.
Points to the Card Set Archive on the Magic website; states no game rule.
Decorative icons in the background of the text box (guild and faction icons) "have no effect on game play" and aren't part of the card data.
Information printed below the text box "has no effect on game play"; it's printing information, not part of the Oracle card data the engine uses.
Collector numbers are printing information with no effect on game play.
The rarity letter after the collector number is printing information with no effect on game play.
Promotional information on promotional printings has no effect on game play.
The version information on printings with interchangeable names is printing information; interchangeable names themselves are tested under 201.3.
The set and language codes (and the premium star) are printing information with no effect on game play.
The illustration credit is printing information with no effect on game play.
The legal text (trademark and copyright) is printing information with no effect on game play.
